articles.title: Chameleon Flake
articles.summary: Medium Voronoi flake mosaic; each cell random metallic brightness, inter-flake gaps, chameleon shimmer. A glittery sparkle in the highlights that becomes a slightly grainy sheen; the flakes themselves are too small to count.
articles.what: ChromaFlair / chameleon flake spec — medium-scale Voronoi (20-40/unit), each flake random metallic value (160-220/255) by hash, random-metallic mosaic pattern, inter-flak Up close: Fine random speckle of bright flake points, each a few pixels wide, scattered unevenly through the highlight band. No visible cell outlines at this size; it reads as glitter in the shine, much stronger on the metallic half. From a distance: A glittery sparkle in the highlights that becomes a slightly grainy sheen; the flakes themselves are too small to count. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: the channels set by its defaults. Group: Exotic & Kinetic (Legacy collection tab of the spec overlay picker). Texture detail: micro.
how: Click a zone card and expand SPEC OVERLAYS.
Click + ADD SPEC OVERLAY, open the Legacy collection tab and the group "Exotic & Kinetic", or search for "Chameleon Flake".
Click it, then click Add this overlay in the Inspect surface window.
Set Strength (default 50%) and tick the Metallic, Roughness and Clearcoat boxes you want.
Use Size and Rotation to make the texture finer, then render.
tips: Hood, roof, doors: broad panels show the glitter in sun
Pair under color-shift or candy paints
Numbers stay clear; flake adds sparkle across them, so keep them bold.
Faint sparse sparkle in the highlight; easy to miss
Pairs well with: gloss, metallic, chrome.
pitfalls: Not colour-shift paint: it never changes hue, only sparkle
Not the chameleon paint pattern: no colour travel is added
Avoid: needs gloss base to shimmer, can look noisy on matte.
articles.intent_note: A spec pattern changes the shine only: metal, roughness and clearcoat, never the paint colour.
articles.paint_advice: It cannot recolour anything. Metal added to a light paint looks bright; metal added to a dark paint stays dark, because metal reflection inherits the paint colour. Pair it with a paint that gives the gloss difference something to show on.

combos.why: Up to five overlays stack in order; a strong overlay can wash out the ones below it.
The blend mode decides how this overlay meets the base shine. Normal is the safe start.
Coat values 1 to 15 and roughness under 15 on non-chrome pixels are raised to safe values on export.

examples.result: The shine of the zone gets this texture while the colours stay put.

articles.title: Damascus Steel Spec
articles.summary: Flow-distorted layer bands, high-carbon bands polish bright against smooth low-carbon bands; watery wavy sheen. A soft watery shimmer across the highlight; the fine lines vanish and leave a gently marbled sheen.
articles.what: Damascus steel surface micro-topography spec — flow-field distorted layer bands, high-carbon bands (R=190/255 metallic, G=20/255 smooth, polishes bright), low-carbon band Up close: Fine wavy, flowing striations, 3-6 px apart, that wander and swirl like watered silk or a folded-steel blade, with small whorls where the lines bend. Visible as shimmery ripple inside the highlight on both halves, slightly crisper on metallic. From a distance: A soft watery shimmer across the highlight; the fine lines vanish and leave a gently marbled sheen. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: the channels set by its defaults. Group: Exotic & Kinetic (Legacy collection tab of the spec overlay picker). Texture detail: micro.
how: Click a zone card and expand SPEC OVERLAYS.
Click + ADD SPEC OVERLAY, open the Legacy collection tab and the group "Exotic & Kinetic", or search for "Damascus Steel Spec".
Click it, then click Add this overlay in the Inspect surface window.
Set Strength (default 50%) and tick the Metallic, Roughness and Clearcoat boxes you want.
Use Size and Rotation to make the texture finer, then render.
tips: Hood, roof and sides on metallic or chrome bases so the ripple shows
Long smooth panels where the flow lines can travel
Numbers stay fully readable; the ripple is gentle.
A faint watered ripple in the highlight, subtle
Pairs well with: metallic, gloss, chrome, matte.
pitfalls: Not a damascus paint pattern: it adds no grey or etched colour contrast, only shine variation
Not brushed metal: lines swirl and flow rather than run straight
Avoid: needs gloss to show bands, washes out on flat matte.

articles.title: Liquid Metal
articles.summary: Near-mirror liquid surface with two-frequency gravity wave interference; standing wave beating makes slow ripples roll across the shine. Reads as a smooth, slightly wet-looking silver sheen; the ripples fade and what remains is a strong clean highlight on metal.
articles.what: Mercury / liquid metal surface — near-perfect reflectivity (R: 240-255, G: 2-8, B: 16-18) with two-frequency gravity wave interference pattern, standing wave beating crea Up close: On satin it is mostly smooth with sparse tiny dark scratch-like flecks and thin hairline arcs. On the metallic base the highlight turns bright and silvery, with fine interference ripples, like water rings, rolling through the band. From a distance: Reads as a smooth, slightly wet-looking silver sheen; the ripples fade and what remains is a strong clean highlight on metal. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: the channels set by its defaults. Group: Exotic & Kinetic (Legacy collection tab of the spec overlay picker). Texture detail: micro.
how: Click a zone card and expand SPEC OVERLAYS.
Click + ADD SPEC OVERLAY, open the Legacy collection tab and the group "Exotic & Kinetic", or search for "Liquid Metal".
Click it, then click Add this overlay in the Inspect surface window.
Set Strength (default 50%) and tick the Metallic, Roughness and Clearcoat boxes you want.
Use Size and Rotation to make the texture finer, then render.
tips: Hood, roof and doors: wide smooth panels show the ripples in the highlight
Fenders and bumpers on a metallic base for the mercury feel
Numbers read cleanly; ripples are low contrast.
Barely changes it; a few faint hairline flecks, still reads satin
Pairs well with: gloss, chrome, metallic, satin.
pitfalls: Not a chrome base: it changes the spec texture, a plain chrome base is cleaner and flatter
Not a colour: no silver paint is added, the car keeps its colour
Avoid: matte bases that flatten the mirror, heavy graphics that break the ripple.
